brief:
Settlers uprooted ancient olive trees in Douma, a village south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank, the Shehab Wire reported. The trees, some of them centuries old, represent a critical economic and cultural resource for Palestinian families in the area who depend on olive cultivation for their livelihoods.

The destruction adds to a documented pattern of settler-led assaults on Palestinian agricultural infrastructure across the territory. Douma residents have endured repeated incursions targeting their olive groves, which remain among the most economically vital assets available to farming communities in the region.
